thread:
maya: Heads-up — Greystone wants a quick POC to migrate from CompetitorX to Redwood. Main asks: prompt parity, streaming shape (they expect a `done` frame + session_state), token billing comparability, and a short security questionnaire. Target window: two weeks. Can we scope effort and POC cost?

samir: I can handle the adapter. CompetitorX protocol: final stream frame includes {"done": true, "session_state": {...}}. They rely on client-side rehydrate. Our streaming yields token chunks and keeps KV cache server-side, no session blob returned by default.

rachel: Runtime can emit a compat envelope when header `X-Redwood-Compat: competitorx-compat` is present. We'll add a final control frame with compat fields and an explicit `done:true`. Estimate: 1.5 dev days + 0.5 QA.

samir: Adapter plan: intercept streaming frames, buffer token chunks, reassemble into frames that match their contract, append session_state at end (we'll synthesize from KV snapshot). Prototype: 6-8 hrs.

evan: Pricing sketch for hosted POC: assume 10M tokens gen / month. Retail example rate $0.00075/token -> $7,500/mo. Offer: 20% POC credit -> ~$6,000 for trial month. If they want Dedicated, give commit options + lead time.

trevor: Legal note — Greystone asked for a clause covering output deltas and liability caps. I'll loop Legal. We probably add SOW language: we don't guarantee byte-for-byte parity, will provide migration support and one rollback window.

legal-bot: Triage: need exact SOW phrasing before customer signatures. Suggest "best-effort parity" + 30-day reconciliation for billing variances.

sec-bot: Security checklist: https://redwood-internal/sec-templates/quick-sq. Customer wants SOC2 + BYOK + EU data residency. For POC: we can host in eu-west-1 staging and enable cross-account KMS; Private deployment requires SOW + ~3-4 week lead.

maya: Webhook/delivery parity? CompetitorX includes `request_id` per event and client dedupes.

samir: We'll echo `request_id` and add `X-Redwood-Request-Id` in webhook headers. Webhooks are at-least-once. Document recommended dedupe by `request_id`.

rachel: Token counting: different tokenizers -> expect ~1-5% variance. We'll offer a reconciliation window and a small billing credit if POC variance >10%.

ev an: (typo) sorry — Evan here. Also check streaming ordering spikes. If adapter buffers to build final frame we may add 50-200ms tail latency on small responses. Call it out.

samir: Test matrix I propose:
- 1k canonical prompts through CompetitorX and Redwood shim
- measure token_count delta, response token diff, ngram similarity, and streaming reassembly success
- flag >15% semantic or >10% token delta for manual review
- smoke test webhooks and idempotency

maya: Deploy notes for POC (for handoff):
```bash
# enable compat shim on staging in eu-west-1
redwood config set region eu-west-1
redwood config set compat competitorx-compat
redwood deploy --env staging --staging-ttl 7d
```

deploy-bot: provisioned staging greystone-poc in eu-west-1 -> 3.120.46.22 (expires in 7d).

trevor: Action items: Samir prototype adapter (1 day), Rachel enable compat header + QA (2 days), Evan send POC pricing email + credit offer, Maya schedule kickoff with customer, Legal to draft SOW clause, Sec to send SQ. Meeting Thu 11am to sync.

maya: I'll prepare a short customer-facing bullet email: timeline, estimated cost, residency options, and known deltas (tokenization + 50-200ms stream tail). Will post draft here. :thumbsup:
